parameters: Pinned to the door: "Mending only. No cloth till the cart comes."
The door is locked.
A dog barks behind the door. Nobody comes.
Someone inside says, "Not today, thank you."
The door is barred.
Through the shutters: a family at supper. Better not.
Locked.
"No lamp oil," says the sign. It has been underlined twice.
A loom clacks inside, then stops.
Nobody comes to the door.
A child peeks out of the window above, then ducks away.
A woman's voice: "If you're selling something, we've no coin."
Nobody answers.
The door is locked.
A dog barks behind the door. Nobody comes.
\C[6]Lilydale\C[0]
North: Hollow Wood.
North: Hollow Wood, then Mistveil.
Carved under it, very old: a small rose.
MARKET DAY - every seventh day, in Rose Square.
Pinned below, newer: "Has anyone seen Hanna from the villa?"
The stones are worn smooth where a hundred years of hands have rested.
Flour dust in the cracks of the counter, and nothing else.
This was where the villa's cart unloaded.
An old tree with leaves the colour of wine.
Children have carved their names into the bark, low down.
One name is carved higher than the others, as if by someone who never grew any taller.
White lilies. The village was named for them, or they for the village -
nobody remembers which came first.
\C[6]Old Bram:\C[0]
We used to play under this tree, the lot of us.
Funny. I can't remember my own wedding, but I remember that.
\C[6]Old Marta:\C[0]
The villa folk always came on market day.
Three weeks now. Not even Hanna with her basket.
\C[6]Shepherd:\C[0]
Two ewes dead in the north pasture. Not a mark on the wool.
Folk say it's the villa. I say it's something out of that wood.
\C[6]Young Mother:\C[0]
The priest from the road says the house in the mist is cursed.
My gran says it was the kindest house in the valley.
\C[6]Tavern Regular:\C[0]
Ale's gone thin since the villa stopped buying.
Funny how a house nobody visits keeps a whole village fed.
\C[6]Greengrocer:\C[0]
Apples, greens, the last of the oranges.
Buy something, would you? Half the square's gone quiet.
\C[6]Bell-Ringer:\C[0]
Every spring we ring the bell for the lady of the villa.
She was born two lanes from here, you know. Married the quiet gentleman from the hill.
Grandpa says a vampire used to give him sweets!
I think he's making it up.
\C[6]Girl:\C[0]
Don't go in the wood. The mist eats sound.
Mama says so.
\C[6]Gardener:\C[0]
Lilies don't care who comes to market.
Wish I could say the same for the rest of us.
The cat stretches on the warm stones.
